judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX (rank 0) Indicators in Chapter 12 – Sound within the 'Moving things, People and Ideas' Content Domain, judged at the same Indicator grain. C188 has the learner experimentally verify that sound propagation requires a medium (LC tags: experiment, medium, propagation, sound); C197 has the learner explain how the density of that medium affects propagation (LC tags: density, propagation, sound). Establishing empirically that a material medium is necessary is the conceptual foundation for reasoning about how a property of the medium (density) governs propagation, so same-rank direction is supported by substantive content, not merely shared chapter, page 46 proximity, or overlapping 'sound/propagation' wording. Note the endpoints sit under different parents (CLO83 investigation-focused vs CLO84 explanation-focused), which is consistent with a verify-then-explain progression rather than contradicting it. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and merge/audit context attaches to several ancestors, so the judgment rests on the bounded descriptions, codes, coordinates, and LCs supplied.

This is complementary conceptual/representational reinforcement rather than a demonstrable dependency, and at equal rank the evidence does not substantiate a developmental direction either way (the shared token overlap is limited to 'reflex'), so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (rank 0, same canonical coordinate) under the same Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome CLO76 ('Differentiates various forms of energy, power & average power') in Chapter 11 – Work and Energy. C173 distinguishes the three quantities work, energy and power; C171 distinguishes kinetic from potential energy qualitatively and mathematically through examples. These are complementary discriminations within the same energy-concept cluster: one separates work/energy/power as distinct quantities, the other partitions mechanical energy into its forms, so they reinforce a common conceptual base without either being substantively required for the other. Same-rank placement provides no directional evidence, and the texts give no pair-specific evidence that proficiency in one materially raises likelihood of success in the other, so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (rank 0) under NCERT LO7 ('Draws labelled diagrams... cell organelles and tissues'), so the grain and statement type match. C76 (Chapter 5, The fundamental unit of life) has learners prepare stained temporary mounts of onion peel and cheek cells, record observations, and draw labelled diagrams of those cells; C97 (Chapter 6, Tissues) requires labelled diagrams of complex permanent tissues (xylem, phloem) and their associated elements. The pair-specific change is a shift from single-cell observation and representation to representing multicellular tissue organisation composed of specialised cell types, so first-hand microscopic observation and accurate cell-level labelled drawing in C76 supports success in the more complex tissue-level diagrammatic work of C97. Same-rank direction rests on this substantive cell-to-tissue extension of the same representational skill, not merely on shared LO7 parentage or shared 'draws labelled diagram' wording. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 and 24 omitted source-evidence items) and several ancestors carry merge/audit context, so the judgment relies on the bounded descriptions and LCs supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class IX NCERT Learning Outcomes (same statement-type grain, same canonical coordinate 'Class IX', rank 0, same parent Class node), so any developmental direction would need substantive same-rank evidence. LO1 is a classification/differentiation process skill (prokaryote vs eukaryote, distance vs displacement, speed vs velocity, element/compound/mixture, solution/suspension/colloid), while LO6 is a quantitative calculation skill over partly overlapping content (distance, velocity, speed, concentration of solution, boiling points for separation from a mixture). judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 0, no forward developmental gap). C244 describes causes and impact of water pollution including fertiliser runoff from farming (Content Domain Natural Resources, Chapter 14), while C269 analyses/interprets graphical data on crop yields in relation to nutrient levels after fertiliser application (Content Domain Food, Chapter 15). Their coherence is substantive rather than merely lexical: both address the consequences of fertiliser application in agriculture, C269 on the productivity side and C244 on the environmental-cost side, so they reinforce a common fertiliser-use concept from complementary perspectives. The cognitive demands differ markedly (descriptive explanation of pollution sources versus graphical data analysis), the ancestor paths are entirely distinct apart from the shared Class IX organizer, and shared-token evidence is thin (jaccard ~0.10, shared value 'fertiliser'), so proficiency in either does not measurably support success in the other; no same-rank developmental direction is justified. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all ancestors carry merge/audit context, so this rests on the bounded excerpts only.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements at the same Class IX coordinate (rank 0) within Chapter 12 – Sound. C209 ('Uses SI units for the concepts under sound') and C204 ('Draws wave graphs showing pitch, loudness and intensity') sit under different Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome parents (CLO86 on SI units vs CLO85 on labelled diagrams/graphs) and under different NCERT LO ancestors, so neither is a decomposition of the other. They are substantively complementary sound-representation skills: quantitative units for sound quantities (frequency, amplitude/intensity) support and are naturally used when labelling and interpreting wave graphs of pitch, loudness and intensity. Same-rank placement and the evidence provided (shared Chapter/Content Domain, single shared LC token 'sound', weak page/rank proximity) give no substantive basis for asserting a developmental direction either way, so symmetric coherence is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes (CLO66, CLO68) in the same grain, sharing the Chapter 'Heredity and Evolution' and Content Domain 'The World of the Living', but hanging from different NCERT LO parents (LO15 initiative to know scientific discoveries; LO17 honesty/objectivity/freedom from myth). Substantively they are complementary affective/scientific-temper outcomes about the same subject matter: taking initiative to learn Darwin's contributions to evolution, and applying objectivity and rational thinking to myths/superstitions about heredity and inheritance. This is meaningful conceptual coherence and mutual reinforcement of scientific temper within heredity/evolution, but neither statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other, and the identical Class X rank (gap 0) provides no developmental direction, so no buildsTowards direction is asserted. Token/trigram and page-proximity signals are weak and carry no independent semantic weight. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (rank 0) in the 'Materials' Content Domain that operate on atomic mass: C39 calculates molecular mass of molecules from atomic mass values (Chapter 3 – Atoms and Molecules, under CLO14/LO6 on calculation), while C49 writes atomic mass, atomic number and symbol to represent an element (Chapter 4 – Structure of atoms, under CLO20/LO9 on scientific conventions and symbols). The shared LC tag/text tokens ('atomic', 'mass') reflect genuine conceptual coherence — quantitative use of atomic mass alongside its notational representation — so this is more than generic wording overlap. However, the two sit in different chapters and different parent LO/CLO strands (calculation vs. representation conventions), and the equal Class IX rank supplies no ordering; the chapter sequence (Ch.3 before Ch.4) even runs counter to the intuitive notation-before-calculation reading, so no substantive same-rank developmental direction is warranted. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, but the retained descriptions and codes are unambiguous for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (C93, C95) of the same grain under the same parent CLO35 ('types of plant tissues ... and animal tissues') in Chapter 6 – Tissues, and both are resolved at identical coordinate rank 0 (Class IX). C93 explains the structure and functions of animal tissues (muscle fibres, connective, epithelial, nerve cells), while C95 elaborates the role of meristematic tissue in non-uniform plant growth. They cover complementary, non-overlapping branches of the tissue concept (animal tissue types versus plant meristematic tissue function), so there is substantive conceptual coherence within the tissue topic but no evidence that proficiency in one supports success in the other; same-rank developmental direction is not substantively supported. Shared ancestors, page 32 proximity, and the weak 'tissue' token/LC overlap alone do not establish a dependency. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (32 omitted items each) and both carry upstream merge/code audit context, so a stronger developmental claim cannot be grounded here.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (same grain, same resolved coordinate rank 1) under the Materials Content Domain and the shared NCERT LO5 parent path, so same-rank direction rests on substantive content evidence rather than proximity. C30 (Chapter 3 – Metals and Non-metals, parent CLO9 on properties/reactivity of metals and salt-solution reactions) has learners infer metal reactivity from experimental results and arrange metals in decreasing order of reactivity, establishing the empirical reactivity series. C55 (Chapter 5 – Periodic classification, parent CLO16 on features of the modern periodic table and reactivity by position) requires explaining how that reactivity series is linked to atomic structure and position in the Modern Periodic Table — a theoretical account of the ordering C30 produces. Learning-component evidence corroborates this (C30: 'infers the reactivity of metals based on experimental results', 'arranges metals in decreasing order of reactivity'; C55: 'explains how the reactivity series of metals is linked to their atomic structure' and 'relates reactivity of metals to their position in the Periodic Table'). Proficiency in establishing and ordering the reactivity series supports success in explaining it structurally, so the developmental direction runs from the second SFI (C30) to the first (C55). Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and both carry upstream merge/audit context, but the retained descriptions, codes, and LCs are consistent and sufficient for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (same statement-type grain, same numeric rank 1) in the Content Domain 'How things work' and both concern the electric motor. C211 (under CLO92, Chapter 13 Magnetic Effect of Electric Current) is a qualitative explanation of the role of the various components of an electric motor/generator; C191 (under CLO83, Chapter 12 Electricity) is a quantitative application, calculating the power of a motor using an appropriate formula and unit. The shared substance is the motor as a device, but the two skills sit in different parent learning outcomes (explanation of working principles vs numerical calculation) and neither text shows that proficiency in one substantively supports success in the other; identifying component roles does not supply the electric-power computation skill, and computing motor power does not deepen component-role explanation. With equal rank there is no rank-based direction and no substantive same-rank developmental evidence, so the coherent complementary pairing is recorded as symmetric relatedness. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (including merged Chapter, Content Domain, and LO organizers), which limits but does not contradict this reading; shared Class, Content Domain, and the single 'motor' LC token alone were not treated as establishing a relation.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators (C57, C47) at the same Class IX coordinate (rank 0) under the shared Chapter 'Structure of atoms' in the Materials content domain, but they sit under different Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome parents (CLO22 on the Thomson-to-Bohr model journey; CLO18 on isotopes and isobars) and different NCERT LOs (LO15, LO5). C57's learning components concern the Bohr model of electron arrangement and its correction of Rutherford's drawbacks; C47's components concern describing isotopes/isobars and their uses, which rest on nucleon composition (atomic/mass number) rather than on the Bohr electron-shell model. The two are coherent, complementary facets of atomic structure within one chapter, so meaningful conceptual coherence exists, but the evidence does not show that proficiency in the Bohr model substantively supports success with isotopes/isobars (or the reverse), and same-rank developmental direction would require substantive evidence that is absent here. Both SFIs' source evidence is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, further limiting any directional claim.
